title: Day 7 of my paper-trading bot competition: Strategy 9 is a beast still +$1,608.66 (+32.17%)
author: DadsGamesandCharles
selftext:
Quick recap for anyone new: over the past year I've built a bunch of AI trading bots, and on Oct 22 I started a public paper-money competition with 13 accounts at $5,000 each (10 strategies, an account that follows Charles 2.0, which is a prediction engine that posts its up-picks before the open, an AI agent's account called Brokgot, and my own hand-traded account). This is the day 7 update, covering everything through the Oct 30 close, which also wraps up the first full week.

https://i.redd.it/skw7x2zi8oyh1.png

https://i.redd.it/ge966x2l8oyh1.png

Everything below is paper money. Nobody steps in to fix the accounts.

Brokgot made its first trade in a few days: it shorted 189 shares of RIVN at $11.96 a few minutes after the open, then bought them all back at $11.93 at 3:50 PM. RIVN swung both ways after it got in, from about $11.53 up to $12.27, so a small $5.67 gain was a decent way out of that one.



SPY for comparison



SPY, close to close: Oct 22 -1.18%, Oct 23 -0.52%, Oct 26 +0.71%, Oct 27 +0.56%, Oct 28 +0.34%, Oct 29 -0.38%, Oct 30 -1.77%. From the Oct 21 close to the Oct 30 close, SPY is down about 2.25%. Over the same stretch the 10 strategies combined are up 7.59% in paper dollars, and the 10 strategies plus Charles 2.0 are up 7.11%.



Today, Oct 30: a red day



Not every day is going to look like yesterday. SPY fell 1.77% today, its worst day since the competition started, and the 10 strategies combined gave back $816.30. Four strategies still finished green (Strategy 3, 4, 6 and 10) and six finished red. Charles 2.0 lost $125.24.



Most of the damage came from FCEL. It popped right at the open and faded fast, and nearly every account that traded it took a loss. The accounts that also traded AMD mostly made that back, with one big exception: Strategy 5 lost $398.82 on AMD, which turned it from slightly green to the bottom of the board. Strategy 2 had the other rough one, -$356.82, all on FCEL.



On the good side, Strategy 10 made $61.59 and moved up to second place overall, and Strategy 3, 4 and 6 all added to their totals on a day when the market was down. Strategy 9 lost $87.24 but is still well out in front at +32.17%.

How Charles 2.0's picks did today



There were four picks today. For each one I checked whether the stock's high for the day, between the 9:30 AM open and 3:59 PM, reached +0.25%, +0.5% and +1.0% above the 9:30 AM open, using minute bars.



1. AMD: high +2.24% above the open. Touched all three levels.

2. MDB: high +0.18% above the open. Didn't reach any of the three levels.

3. FCEL: high +2.69% above the open. Touched all three levels.

4. LABU: high +5.41% above the open. Touched all three levels.



So three of four touched +0.25%, +0.5% and +1.0%, and MDB never really got going. FCEL is a good reminder that a pick can do its job and a trade can still lose: it reached +2.69% within the first couple of minutes, but most of the accounts didn't catch that move.



Running tally for live Charles 2.0 picks, Sep 22 through Oct 30 (29 sessions, 116 picks): 102 touched +0.25% above the open (88%), 93 touched +0.5% (80%), and 75 touched +1.0% (65%). What I care about is whether a pick reaches those levels during the day, since I want the money that same day, not the next.



Keeping it honest



Seven sessions is still a short stretch, and some people have had doubts about the strategies, which is fair. That's exactly why this is happening in public, red days included. If the bots fall behind SPY over a real stretch, I'll say so right here.



A few people asked about the strategy: I'm keeping the exact rules to myself, but the bots all start from the same morning picks and differ in how they get in and out.



What's next



Daily results after each close, and a fuller write-up as the sample grows. See you Monday.



Questions you probably have



Is this real money? No. Every account is paper money.



Is paper trading realistic? Not entirely. Paper can't show market impact, and real fills are usually worse. That's the main reason my early backtests got cut down.



Will you ever trade real money? Yes, we will.



Can I buy or subscribe to anything? Not yet.



Is this financial advice? No. The picks are research ideas to watch, not tips, and nothing here is a guarantee of anything.



Are AI agents involved? Yes. AI agents help build, test and run the bots, and one of the accounts is traded by an AI agent. I'm the one who reviews and posts this.



Why publish bad numbers? Because a track record that only shows the good days isn't worth much.



What if a bot loses? Then it loses in public. The accounts are paper and no one steps in to fix them.



Why did the competition start on Oct 22? Earlier starts on Monday and Tuesday had account setup problems, so those days don't count.



Where can I follow along? On this profile. I'll post daily results here after the close.



Have a question that isn't here? Ask in the comments and I'll answer it.



Paper money only. Not financial advice. Written with help from AI.

replies.author: DadsGamesandCharles
replies.body:
I don't trade Forex much, but a lot of ICT concepts are really just supply-and-demand and liquidity concepts. Those ideas can show up in any liquid market, including FX, stocks, futures, and crypto. The question isn't whether ICT 'works' as a package, it's which specific concepts give a measurable edge.

To me at least. Also, the actual patterns will vary across each one of those. I'm used to stocks so I know how to read pretty much any graph, but I tried to do that with crypto and I would have lost the farm because the foundations of the concept didn't hold up, even though the foundation is built on the same things you look for.

I could make Charles work for anything, it just depends on how much I know about it and how much new stuff he would have to build in order for him to have that as an option. Then I;d have to tweak it for optimal effeciency. I did that with some puts and call bots, but I don;t know enough about puts and calls to really care too much to advance that project.

replies.author: Enzobevmax
replies.body:
I want to stress that your objective in posting is great. I think we all value the most, though, from transparency and a "leveling with one another" that makes us all on the same team. I applaud anyone who has made progress in this area as it bodes well for others(like me!!) to do the same in their own way so please don't take this as an attack.

Reddit bringing down setup descriptions is very odd. I have been blocked by a few subs for my posts appearing to self-promoting like I am selling something(maybe one day(??) ha) so maybe that's it but I really think there is a lot of value and validity you can bring to everyone by sharing even a few details. 

Apples to oranges, I know but here are two of the top performing intraday setups I have for my random setup generator I toy with:

1. Late-Day Choppy Dip Buy (SPY red)

When: between 2:00 and 3:00 PM, and only if SPY is down more than 0.5% from its open.

What to look for: a stock that trades at least $50M a day, and has spent the day chopping back and forth across VWAP (8 or more crosses since 9:50). It has just dropped sharply: RSI fell 5½+ points in 15 minutes, and price sits 1.7%+ below its 50-bar average on the 5-minute chart.

Trade: buy at the close of that 5-minute bar. “1 unit” is a quarter of the stock’s normal daily range (ATR). Put the stop 1 unit below your entry and the target 1 unit above. If neither is hit, sell by 3:55 PM. One trade per stock per day.

Idea: a choppy stock that gets pushed too far down on a red afternoon tends to snap back toward its average.

2. Late-Day New-Low Buy (SPY red)

When: between 2:00 and 3:00 PM, and only if SPY is down more than 0.25% from its open.

What to look for: a stock that trades at least $150M a day, steadily falling (its 20-bar average on the 5-minute chart has sloped down 0.28%+ over the last 25 minutes), that just made a new low of the day.

Trade: buy that new low. Stop 1 unit below, target 1 unit above, out by 3:55 PM. One trade per stock per day.

Idea: late-day new lows on a down day often get bought by dip buyers and short sellers taking profits before the close.

I had claude produce these based on my data so they are a little more complex than their true executions but I think viewers might see these and trigger other thoughts to have about their own strategies.

replies.author: DadsGamesandCharles
replies.body:
These are good, a bit more complex than Charles, but that’s only because of what you’re doing vs what he’s doing.

The complexity might be hurting you though and if you can trim that down (all the deterministic factors) it might help. Complexity meaning you have a LOT of criteria to meet in your algos before something happens.

I see where you’re going with it and it’s not bad, not wrong, it’s pretty good actually, but to me, it’s way too complex. Maybe that’s because I don’t know what happens behind the scenes but with that many deterministic factors I’m going toto bet the farm if you shrink it down you’ll increase your profit.

I say that because it LOOKS like you’re scanning the entire market to find your target, are you?

replies.author: Enzobevmax
replies.body:
Great tidbit and you're right. Complexity and not handicapping or restricting our setups is something I look into weekly. If you can, take a look at my recent weekend post

Among a few other things, I have a built-in portion of the mission statement saying something like, if we are carving a statue out of a block, we don't want to keep cutting and carving until there is little or nothing left.

To answer you, every minute, the system checks 3,000+ liquid US stocks and ETFs(a bespoke selection of ours based on a few volume metrics) against every live setup’s rules. It acts only at each 5-minute bar close, then the safeguards decide which signals trade.

Love the chat!

replies.author: Enzobevmax
replies.body: Sorry but can you elaborate on how your setups are more simple? May help a lot of us!

replies.author: DadsGamesandCharles
replies.body:
Your first strategy has like 10 different deterministic factors to take into consideration, and that’s not even counting for the factors that have to be hit in order for the ones you’re looking for to even exist.

The idea/logical conclusion behind it holds up but how you’re getting there may be hurting you because you’re trying to cover ALL the bases when you really only need to cover a few of them.

The stock market, everything about it, plays off each other so if you can determine which factors you’re using that play off each other, you can take your criteria from say, 10, down to 5 or 7 and those 5 or 7 will benefit you more.

KISS

That’s a big rule of mine when I’m building because dealing with the agent is already like trying to chase a golden retriever in a fireworks store so if I can alleviate any steps, we both benefit.

replies.author: Enzobevmax
replies.body:
Definitely understand what you mean and thats definitely a main focus of ours is to be as least restricting as possible while also not casting too wide of a net. Also have to consider each set up is searched over 3,000 tickers every minute so the thought is we can sacrifice a little constriction if searched that many times.

Can you provide an example of what an average setup of yours looks like for reference?

replies.author: DadsGamesandCharles
replies.body:
I'll try and answer this as best I can and it roles into something you said.

Charles doesn't need to search 3000 tickers every minute, more is not always more and with data, more can just dilute the results.

It would make sense, to me, to scan that many if they were all worth scanning. If you had a gold mine, you'd be happy when an emerald was found, but you're trying to run a gold mine, not a gem mine.

But you had to find that mine first right? So you gotta figure out what you really need to look for in order to find your gold. And, key point, you don't usually find gold everywhere.

comments.author: TrustedEssentials
comments.body:
You mentioned Strategy 9 uses a “dip chain.” Could you explain the basic structure without giving away your strategy? Does it buy a dip, sell the rebound, then wait for another dip, or can it add to an existing position as the price falls?

Also, how does it handle a stock that keeps falling instead of bouncing? No need for exact indicators or thresholds. I’m just interested in understanding the mechanics.

replies.author: DadsGamesandCharles
replies.body:
These are great questions.

The dip chain is exactly how it sounds, a chain of dips. It can only be pulled off if the first buy is successful. If it’s not the entire strategy is done for the day.

And you know what, because this is such a great question and because somebody else said that everything was a lot of bluster, I’m gonna go into a little more detail than usual.

The beginning of this strategy begins the day before at the close. Charles decides whether or not that day is going to be good for the next day. Keep this in mind, if a stock is up it’s going to go down and historically if it’s up at close, it’s going to go down in the morning.

Do not take that as it staying down in the morning because that is not what I said.

Charles can create a dip chain because of that, he can also reverse engineer it, and that’s as much as I can tell you about how that particular strategy works. 

Most of these strategies don’t have a stop loss and if they do, it’s very high. The max draw down for the strategies I believe is anywhere between eight and 34% possibly even 50% but I can’t tell you for certain right now as I don’t have the data in front of me.

Now those drawdowns sound ridiculously high and you probably wonder why would anybody want that, and the answer is that I don’t want that, but unfortunately, more risk equals more profit. With all of these accounts, I can step in at any time and hit the cell button or by any stock that I want and have Charles manage it for me, but if I do that it It contains the data because it’s not actually AI trading it. I say that to say that at any point, I can stop the losses on any of these accounts, but that would also mean I would stop the profits too sometimes.

replies.author: spoidercide
replies.body:
My point is the test's value would have been a lot more valuable if you were able to collect real world micro-size run profitability. Simulated slippage and fees does not give you an accurate or real fill inside the order book.

You can only put up what you're willing to lose and by solely paper trading you're willing to lose nothing.

It's definitely better risk management than blindly aping into things but live profitability is on a per strategy per regime basis. If you're here to stay for the long term you will be working hard just like any other day trader constantly monitoring adjusting accounting for and building multiple combinant parallel strategies to reduce aggregate risk and exposure.

That's at least my interpretation of how to do it on an institutional level.

There's less value in trying to find 1 runner that does exceptionally well and then gamble into him after regimes change from a 1 of 1 paper run vs an interoperable swarm of runners.

The whole mentality of picking a singular agent and handing them cash is outright ridiculous in my opinion.

Nobody wants to lay it flat out:

AI at best will weakly interpret an algorhythm and be very temporary.

Willingness to learn how to possess coded, meticulously selected parameter tuned multi regime asset class specific cluster strategies that seek aggregate 10+% turnarounds in multiple markets because of focus on mean reversion, upward trending, breakout, downward trending, liquidity sweeps etc thats how it this game really works.

If you want to feel safe it will take a lot more work than giving an AI agent money.

Until you genuinely built it yourself or put real money into it you will have only dipped your toes in a place where the sharks are eating each other alive all day.

The sentiment is there and you're in the right places with the right mindset.

But don't think this is ever going to be easy.

Entering the market is easy, knowing when to take profits or just break even becomes more difficult.

If $1000 makes strategy 9 "a beast"  
and you're this excited just posting these things rather than genuinely risking what you're willing to lose to learn

It's a good sign you're not ready for what it really feels like the first time you're looking at numbers on your screen that make a day job feel worthless.

Good luck I think as long as you continue to have fun with it and enjoy the process you will make a great trader algorhythmically agentically or however you prefer it

  
EDIT:

bonus tip my friend thank you for reading all this..

build for prop firms and cap your risk while increasing your profit threshhold

if you can build your trading strategy to quantitatively pull money out of prop firms you will truly have good strategies that can be relied upon to never lose more than they make
